runners_data.name: Chairmanfourtimes
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong finishing kick who should benefit from the expected strong gallop
runners_data.comment: Best form when winning 5f Listed race (soft) as 2yo; well held since; now tongue tied

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: Front-runner making turf debut after two AW wins, likely to set a strong pace from the start
runners_data.comment: Made all for two 5f AW wins; good 4th on turf debut at York; open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: All three runs in these aids; made all for two 5f wins on Southwell AW before giving it a good shot on turf debut in a competitive York handicap (5f, good) in May, when just behind Naana's Shadow; open to improvement but lack of experience raises a question on this tricky track.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent form who can track the pace and finish well if positioned correctly
runners_data.comment: Had plenty of chances in handicaps but good 4th at Goodwood puts him on the scene
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win in 6f novice on Kempton AW as 2yo; has had plenty of chances in handicaps, albeit with his persevering fourth to Wedonttelllies at Goodwood 13 days ago, when switched across the track, putting him on the scene here with the expected strong pace likely to suit; cheekpieces refitted.

runners_data.name: Riley Rocks
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose two wins came over 6f but showed ability when staying on at Goodwood recently
runners_data.comment: Two 6f wins; coped well with 5f latest despite not getting a clear run; similar worry here
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins over 6f (on AW) but he didn't seem inconvenienced by the return to 5f, despite failing to get a clear passage, at Goodwood recently in the race won by Wedonttelllies; capable of better but he's come from off the pace in three of his four starts which will complicate things in this field.

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow
runners_data.note: Prominent runner under Oisin Murphy who has made all twice this year and handles good ground well
runners_data.comment: Improved as 3yo; useful front-running 3rd of 17 at York recently; in the thick of it again
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner as 2yo who has done well for new yard this year, making all from the rail draw at Catterick, then adopting the same tactics at York (5f, good) when losing her lead late on but still finishing a solid third of 17 (just ahead of Shes Got A Brother); in the thick of it.

runners_data.name: Temple Of Athena
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning to preferred 5f trip after disappointing efforts over longer distances
runners_data.comment: All 3 wins at 5f; had excuses since the latest in March; return to 5f handicap should help
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins at 5f, on soft, good to soft and the AW; has had some excuses since the latest in March and the return to a 5f handicap looks in her best interests after she ran in Listed races either side of a modest 6f run at Chester; it's likely she needs to find extra for this, even so.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Prominent performer who won on soft turf recently and has shown respectable AW form this year
runners_data.comment: Appreciated soft ground when 5f winner at Yarmouth latest; up 7lb but rain helpful
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable rather than progressive on AW since a Wolverhampton win in December but he found soft turf to his liking when coming clear of his four rivals at Yarmouth (5f) last month; needs more off 7lb higher in this better race but further rain would help him more than some.

runners_data.name: Hanney Girl
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who led in both wins as 2yo and will ensure a strong early gallop
runners_data.comment: Two 5f wins as 2yo; creditable York run last month; will do well to win off current mark
runners_data.spotlight: Speedy filly who can lead; two 5f wins on good to firm as 2yo but she has run up to form on good to soft; creditable show when fifth of 17 at York last month but she will do well to win this off her current mark.

runners_data.name: Coyy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who overcame trouble to win at Windsor and should benefit from expected honest pace
runners_data.comment: Cosy 5f winner at Windsor after met trouble; slowly away when creditable 3rd at Goodwood
runners_data.spotlight: Looked ahead of his mark when returned to 5f at Windsor (good to firm) in May, doing well to overcome a blocked passage, and a subsequent third behind Wedonttelllies at Goodwood (5f, good) after a slow start was creditable; has possibilities if he doesn't give himself too much to do.

runners_data.name: Proof
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose stamina-sapping Southwell win suggests the strong gallop will suit his style perfectly
runners_data.comment: Has won on heavy; won his return over 5f on AW; others likely to have brighter early speed
runners_data.spotlight: Heavy-ground winner as 2yo; started the year with a 5f Southwell AW win but the style of that success, when stamina finally came into play after he was niggled along from some way out, suggests others will have brighter early speed on the return to 5f; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Wedonttelllies
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer coming off a good Goodwood win who excels when able to finish strongly late
runners_data.comment: AW winner at 7f as 2yo but well suited by drop to 5f when Goodwood winner latest; up 6lb
runners_data.spotlight: All turf races have been on good or quicker but dam's best form was on soft; sole 2yo win was over 7f on the AW; ran well for a long way over 6f at Ascot on second run back and proved thoroughly at home over the new 5f trip at Goodwood (good; first-time cheekpieces) since, racing well within himself and coming clear for an impressive win; up 6lb but has better to come.

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who struggled at York recently but could benefit from return to expected stronger pace
runners_data.comment: Overcame trouble in running for 5f win on AW in April; never involved back on turf at York
runners_data.spotlight: Did well to overcome trouble in running on Southwell AW (5f) in April but she wasn't in such good form at York (5f, good) three weeks ago in her first turf handicap; has something to prove after that.

runners_data.name: Henrythenate
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three AW wins who ran well for long way at Chester before weakening
runners_data.comment: Three AW wins at 5f; creditable show at Chester for new yard; more on his plate today
runners_data.spotlight: Three 5f wins on AW for previous yards, most recently in February, but treading water in that sphere since; ran well for a long way at Chester (5f, good) in May for new trainer but has more on his plate in this company.

runners_data.name: Artista
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 24 days off who has been weighted to struggle against this level
runners_data.comment: Two 5f wins as 2yo; weighted to best this year; well beaten in a Beverley seller latest
runners_data.spotlight: Two 5f wins (good to firm and AW) last summer but she has been weighted to her best this year and was well beaten in a Beverley seller (first-time cheekpieces, now discarded) last month; up against it.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: Front-running mare under 5lb claimer who will help set the pace but faces tough task from high weight
runners_data.comment: Front-runs; best form on AW; well held on Listed return; has work to do off this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; seems to handle most ground but her 5f maiden win at Cork (good to firm) last July was easily bettered by her AW achievements later; dropped right out on her return in a Listed race at Cork (extended 5f, soft) last month and has work to do off this mark back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Alfa Duplicate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with recent AW wins who could benefit if the pace becomes truly testing
runners_data.comment: Hung on to lead at Beverley latest; much bigger question to answer on very different track
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins at 5f/6f this spring; met her match in Call Margot at Southwell (5f, AW) in April but  showed her fighting spirit when refusing to give up her lead back on turf at Beverley (5f, good to soft) since; much bigger question here, up 4lb in a better race on a very different track.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie Frith, Shes Got A Brother and Hanney Girl will ensure a strong gallop from the start over this sharp 5f at Epsom. With 16 runners and three confirmed front-runners, the pace will be honest throughout with no let-up. The sustained gallop will stretch the field and test stamina reserves in the final furlong. This pace dynamic clearly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers who can finish strongly, as the early leaders will face pressure and potentially weaken late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage early and maintain a solid pace throughout
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up perfectly for hold-up horses to close late as the pace-setters weaken in the final furlong. Horses with proven finishing kicks will have ideal conditions to strike in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters manages to steal a march and build an unassailable lead
scenarios.body: Shes Got A Brother or Hanney Girl could use their speed to dominate from the front if they can get first run on their rivals. The winner would need to maintain galloping strength when the closers challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent racers can sit just off the pace and time their challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: Horses like One And Gone or Temple Of Athena could benefit from tracking the leaders before striking at the optimal moment. This scenario rewards tactical speed and the ability to quicken when positioned ideally.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too fast early and compound badly in the final stages
scenarios.body: An overly aggressive early pace could see all three leaders stop dramatically, allowing any horse with reserves to pick up the pieces. This would create a war of attrition favouring stamina over speed.

watchPoints.text: Watch for trouble in running with 16 runners over the sharp 5f Epsom track, particularly affecting hold-up horses like Chairmanfourtimes and Coyy
Monitor how aggressively the three front-runners Rosie Frith, Shes Got A Brother and Hanney Girl engage early as this will determine the pace strength
Observe Oisin Murphy's tactics on Naana's Shadow as he may try to track the leaders rather than make all from a wide draw
Watch for Wedonttelllies to be produced late with his customary strong finish if the pace sets up as expected
Check if any of the prominent runners like One And Gone or Temple Of Athena can secure ideal tracking positions behind the pace-setters

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan

runners_data.comment: Ran well in an admittedly substandard National Stakes at Sandown last time
runners_data.spotlight: Showed his 40-1 win at Bath (5.7f, firm) was no fluke by running well in an admittedly substandard National Stakes at Sandown (5f, good; Listed) where he gave the impression this step back up in trip will suit.

runners_data.name: Possessive

runners_data.comment: Recorded a respected RPR in winning at York and is open to progress to boot

runners_data.name: Havana Flash

runners_data.name: Benefacta

runners_data.spotlight: Caught the eye in making late headway from last place at Chepstow (6f, good to soft; ended up seventh of 12) but the bare form is modest and there's a danger he'll again get too far back.

runners_data.name: Hickory Lad
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner stepping up from 5f, 30 days since last run but consistent record

runners_data.spotlight: Scored with something to spare under 5lb claimer in a maiden (6f, good) at Hamilton, beating five rivals; may show progress and make an impact at this stronger level, with Oisin Murphy booked.

runners_data.spotlight: Out of a 7f winner and proved suited by the step up to that distance at Haydock (good to soft) where he beat his three rivals; something to prove in this much deeper race returned to sprinting.

runners_data.name: Alpe d'Huez

runners_data.comment: Form of ready AW success at Lingfield isn't strong but he's open to progress

runners_data.name: Time And Effort
runners_data.note: Front-runner with weakest form in field, likely pace-maker role for stronger stablemates
runners_data.comment: Brings the worst form, having finished a modest fourth at Musselburgh

runners_data.name: Romidijo

runners_data.spotlight: Took a step forward with rallying third when upped to 6f at Chepstow (good to soft) but recorded an ordinary RPR and needs to show further improvement upped in class.

runners_data.name: Rlasthope

runners_data.name: El Lambo

races.paceDynamic: Hickory Lad, Alpe d'Huez, and Time And Effort will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with Hickory Lad likely to press hardest given his consistent front-running style over 5f. The pace will be searching throughout the 6f with multiple confirmed leaders creating pressure up front. This sustained gallop will stretch the field and test stamina, particularly on the softening ground at Epsom. The strong pace clearly favours hold-up horses and closers who can benefit from the collapse of over-exerted front-runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage early and maintain a searching gallop
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will stretch the field and allow late runners to pick up the pieces as leaders tire in the final furlong. Hold-up horses with proven stamina will thrive as the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Hickory Lad can dictate without serious pressure from the other leaders
scenarios.body: A more controlled pace allows the classiest front-runner to maintain his kick, with Hickory Lad's solid 5f form translating effectively to 6f. His RPR of 92 gives him the edge if not over-pressed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but one horse can track the leaders without fully committing
scenarios.body: A prominent runner gets the perfect trip behind the battling front-runners and has enough left to strike in the final 100 yards. The pace sets it up perfectly for a horse sitting just off the speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too fast too early and all three fade badly
scenarios.body: The leaders burn out before halfway, creating a sprint finish from a crawling pace that suits horses with natural speed over stamina. This scenario heavily favours the unexposed types with raw pace.

watchPoints.text: Hickory Lad and Alpe d'Huez both come from extended breaks (30+ days) and may lack peak fitness for strong pace battle
Time And Effort brings poor form but could set unsustainable fractions that collapse the entire pace scenario
Havana Flash is completely unexposed on turf and her going preference could determine whether she shows her true ability
Possessive and Wild Terrain are both lightly raced improvers who could find significant advancement at this level
Social Spirit stretching out to 6f for the first time may need the experience more than the result

races.name: Betfred Diomed Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Seagulls Eleven
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent form with two French wins this season, 12 days since Longchamp success keeps him sharp
runners_data.comment: Better than ever in two French races this term; reasonably solid in current form
runners_data.spotlight: Appears versatile as regards ground; Group 3 winner at last year's Glorious Goodwood and better than ever in two French races this term, making all at Longchamp (1m Listed) latest; reasonably solid in current form returned to home soil, and further progress is possible.

runners_data.name: Qirat

runners_data.spotlight: Not totally solid on his form since 150-1 success when pacemaker in last year's Sussex Stakes (1m, good); below par in Listed grade in sole run this season; however, record of 3-3 at Goodwood bodes well for this first visit to Epsom, which is a fairly similar track; return to best is plausible.

runners_data.comment: Rallied gamely for Listed honours at Goodwood last time and should remain competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned mostly on good/firmer ground; rallied gamely for Listed honours at Goodwood (1m2f) most recently and, assuming another gritty display is on the way, should remain competitive; top on his peak figure, achieved when defying top weight in last year's Cambridgeshire (1m1f).

runners_data.name: Royal Playwright
runners_data.note: Prominent sort returning after 189-day layoff, placed fourth in this race last year but fitness concern looms
runners_data.comment: Respectable fourth in this contest last year; showed better form over 1m2f/1m3f later on
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable fourth in this contest last year but showed better form, including success in conditions race and third-place finishes at Listed/Group level, over 1m2f/1m3f later in 2025; doesn't seem to be crying out for this drop back in trip on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Ice Max

runners_data.comment: Close second on good ground in this race last year; most wins on softer; major player

runners_data.name: Chancellor
runners_data.note: Prominent type wearing first-time cheekpieces retained, has thrived on artificial surfaces but unproven on turf
runners_data.comment: The query is whether his very useful AW form can be transferred back to turf

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been gelded since last disappointing run, strong Epsom record with two wins at this meeting
runners_data.comment: Record of 2-2 at Epsom includes a success in this race last year; respected back here
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile as regards ground; gelded prior to below-par effort in sole start this term; smart on his day and is 2-2 at Epsom with wins at this meeting for the last two years; beat Ice Max (who received 3lb) by just under 1l in this race 12 months ago and warrants respect back here.

races.paceDynamic: Boiling Point will set the pace from the gates with Seagulls Eleven, Ice Max, and Qirat tracking prominently behind. The front rank lacks genuine speed horses, creating a moderate tempo that builds gradually through Epsom's undulating contours. With no fierce early pressure on Boiling Point, he can dictate terms before the descent to Tattenham Corner where positioning becomes crucial. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours prominent racers who can stay close to the action and avoid traffic problems that will plague the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Boiling Point Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Boiling Point breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure from the prominent pack
scenarios.body: He can measure out fractions to suit his stamina pattern and prove hard to peg back up the hill. The controlled pace makes it difficult for hold-up horses to generate enough late momentum to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Seagulls Eleven or Ice Max decide to challenge Boiling Point early rather than track
scenarios.body: A genuine pace develops that sets up the race for closers, with the early leaders potentially emptying their tanks. Ryan Moore on Skukuza and Sean Levey on Persica benefit from the stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Favours Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches on the turn and runners get blocked for room in the straight
scenarios.body: The prominent horses avoid trouble while hold-up runners struggle to find clear passages. Boiling Point and those tracking him have clear sailing while the back markers get shuffled back further.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves truly pedestrian and the leaders come back dramatically
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with plenty of kick left in the tank for the hill. Skukuza's class tells if he settles properly, while Persica can unleash his finishing speed.

watchPoints.text: Skukuza's early settling - if he pulls hard again like last time, his chances evaporate quickly
Royal Playwright's fitness after 189 days off - any signs of rustiness in the preliminaries are significant
Traffic problems at Tattenham Corner - the tight turn could cause major interference for hold-up horses
Boiling Point's early fractions - if uncontested he can steal a march that proves decisive
Chancellor's response to turf debut - all his recent form has come on artificial surfaces

races.name: Betfred "Nifty 50" Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Liberty Lane

runners_data.name: Dhahabi

runners_data.name: Tycoon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer unraced on softer than good, form pickup at Newmarket suggests he's finding his range
runners_data.comment: Ran on well into a close third at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) last time
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; failed to make a significant impact in his first four handicaps but did so at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) on latest outing, running on well into a close third of 12 off today's mark; return to 1m2f could help and he needs a second look.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Prominent racer struggling on turf recently despite AW success, poor Epsom record counts against
runners_data.comment: Struggled to make an impact in recent AW starts and finished last on York return to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Below form in this race in 2024 and also last April on his only other visit here; had an excellent autumn last year on AW and won again in January, but he's struggled to make an impact in more recent AW starts and finished last at York on return to turf; return to 1m2f would suit if he were in better form but this may be a tough turf mark.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who acts on good to soft, Cesarewitch winner with solid recent form pattern
runners_data.comment: Not on a bad mark but plenty needs to go right if one of his late rushes is to prevail
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on good to soft, much more to prove on soft; won the Cesarewitch at Newmarket (2m2f, good to firm; 10lb higher today) last October and had some very solid AW form over 1m2f-2m this year, prior to tailing off at 50-1 in the Group 3 Ormonde at Chester four weeks ago; he's not on a bad mark but plenty needs to go right if one of his late rushes is to prevail in this.

runners_data.name: Sallaal
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with soft ground form, hooded recently and showed back-to-form effort at this course
runners_data.comment: Upped to 1m2f for a C&D 2nd (good) on return, running on well with too much to do; up 5lb
runners_data.spotlight: Has run respectably on soft; hooded on last two starts, with a back-to-form second of six when stepped up to 1m2f for C&D handicap (good) on 2026 reappearance; raised 5lb since and probably not straightforward but that was a promising effort here from out the back (ran on well with too much to do) and he has to be in serious calculations.

runners_data.name: Alpha Crucis
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong soft ground record, twice runner-up at Epsom including last year
runners_data.comment: Stays 1m2f, has proved himself here and goes well in the mud; strong each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: All four of his wins were on soft or heavy ground, three at Goodwood; runner-up on his only two visits here, including at this meeting (good to soft) last year and he's 1lb lower today; that was over 8.5f and his creditable fifth on reappearance ten weeks ago was in the 1m Lincoln at Doncaster, but he stays 1m2f; strong each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Quai De Bethune
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse unraced on softer than good, 349-day absence major concern despite early promise
runners_data.comment: Last-gasp win at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm); left A Balding for 775,000gns that July
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; London Gold Cup third at Newbury last May was a promising start to handicap life and he built on that with a last-gasp win from out the back at Royal Ascot (again 1m2f on good to firm); unraced since, having left Andrew Balding for 775,000gns that July and been gelded in September; 7lb higher than at Royal Ascot but he's had just six races.

runners_data.name: Hand Of God
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who scored decisively at Newbury three weeks ago, limited soft ground exposure
runners_data.comment: Won by 2l going away at Newbury (1m2f, good) three weeks ago; unraced here or on soft
runners_data.spotlight: Won on good to soft in 2024, unraced on soft; lightly raced for his age but led in the final 1f of 11-runner race at Newbury (1m2f, good) three weeks ago and scored by 2l going away; back up 5lb; how he'll take to this new track and possible soft ground are greater worries but he makes appeal otherwise.

runners_data.name: Have Secret
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with visor fitted, career-high mark after Pontefract win but harder task here
runners_data.comment: Career-high mark after April win; ran poorly in this last year on his only visit to Epsom
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo who has a career-high mark on the strength of his win at Pontefract (1m2f, good; acts on soft/heavy) in April; creditable fifth at York next time but the chief disincentive is probably that he ran poorly in this race last year on his only visit to Epsom.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who acts on good to soft, recent Redcar second suggests he's in good heart
runners_data.comment: Good second of seven at Redcar (1m2f) five weeks ago, keeping on strongly; up 2lb
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on good to soft, unraced on soft; fit from AW and hurdling when good second of seven at Redcar (1m2f) five weeks ago, keeping on strongly; up 2lb and into a better race but needs a second look.

runners_data.name: Great David
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form came on good ground, handicap mark looks challenging now
runners_data.comment: Ninth of 12 at Chester wasn't a greatly auspicious return to handicap; first headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Won on soft as 2yo; reappearance win last April saw him pitched afterwards into Listed and Group events, in which he was initially on the premises but his handicap mark shot up as a result; ninth of 12 to Respond at Chester wasn't a greatly auspicious return to handicap company on reappearance this season and connections now reach for headgear.

runners_data.name: Let's Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose peak efforts on good ground, Chester experience helps for Epsom's undulations
runners_data.comment: Peak efforts have been on good going in the last 13 months; won at Chester on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Won a soft-ground maiden in 2023 but peak efforts have been on good in the last 13 months; unraced here but scored twice over 1m2f at the similar Chester track, including on his only start this season; all three handicap wins were in tight finishes, but he's gone up just 3lb since latest and is likely to be seriously involved if he goes on the ground.

runners_data.name: Spoken Truth
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with competitive recent form, lowest weight provides theoretical advantage
runners_data.comment: Acts on soft; highly competitive in 1m2f handicaps on all three starts for new connections
runners_data.spotlight: Rather disappointing for Dermot Weld in Ireland after winning a soft-ground maiden; has still not added to that 2024 win but he's been highly competitive in 1m2f handicaps on all three starts for new connections, runner-up to an unexposed rival in the Zetland Gold Cup at Redcar (good to firm) 11 days ago; each-way claims again.

races.paceDynamic: Liberty Lane sits as the lone confirmed front runner in this 17-runner handicap, with several prominent racers like Respond, Bolster, and Hand Of God likely to press but not commit early over this stamina-testing trip. The pace will be sustainable rather than frantic, with Liberty Lane allowed to dictate through steady fractions on the testing ground. This creates a tactical race where the winner will need to be produced with a well-timed challenge, clearly favoring hold-up horses who can finish strongly and prominent racers with stamina reserves over pure speed merchants.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays truly moderate and the field remains bunched turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where horses with the strongest turn of foot prevail, particularly those comfortable racing off slow fractions. Patient tactics and good positioning become crucial as the field fans out in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Pays
scenarios.trigger: If Respond, Hand Of God, and Tycoon apply early pressure to Liberty Lane creating honest fractions
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more demanding which suits horses who can travel strongly in the vanguard without getting overly committed early. Those tracking the pace inherit a tactical advantage as the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Liberty Lane Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Liberty Lane gets uncontested early splits and no serious challenge materializes until too late
scenarios.body: The front runner builds an unassailable advantage on ground that rewards stamina over speed, particularly given the testing conditions. Late closers face an impossible task as the leader has too much in reserve.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses with no early pressure and a cavalry charge develops from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: Multiple horses arrive together in a messy finish where draw, luck in running, and jockey judgment become paramount. The race loses its tactical shape entirely as stamina becomes less relevant.

watchPoints.text: Liberty Lane faces no obvious early pressure which could allow him to dictate terms completely and prove hard to peg back
Tycoon and Quai De Bethune are both unraced on softer than good ground which creates significant question marks
Respond's progressive profile suggests he can handle the step up in class despite limited soft ground experience
Several hold-up horses including Great David and Let's Dream may struggle if the pace becomes too slow early
Alpha Crucis has excellent Epsom form including a second here last year on similar ground conditions

races.name: Betfred Oaks (Group 1) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Legacy Link
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong Gosden 14-day record but untested on anything softer than good ground
runners_data.comment: Asserted close home in the Group 3 Musidora at York and she's firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: All four starts on good to firm/good ground; rallied for fourth in a hot running of the Group 1 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket last October on her final 2yo run, and she reappeared with a hard-fought win in the Group 3 Musidora at York (10.2f), asserting close home; there is every chance that she will stay 1m4f and her pedigree provides optimism that she will be effective on slow ground; dam is a sister to Frankel; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Thundering On
runners_data.note: Prominent runner improving with each start, bred to handle this trip but moderate recent trainer form
runners_data.comment: Powered clear in 1m2f Group 3 at Navan in April when upped in trip; she's one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: By Frankel and dam won the 1m2f Group 1 Pretty Polly for connections; she's improved with each of her four starts and comfortably won the Group 3 Salsabil Stakes at Navan (1m2f, good to yielding) in April when upped in trip; has shown promise on heavy ground; powered clear in the final furlong last time, providing hope that she will stay 1m4f, and she's one to consider.

runners_data.name: A La Prochaine
runners_data.note: Hold-up type proven on soft ground but lacks experience with just two career starts
runners_data.comment: Still looked a work in progress when third to Amelia Earhart in Cheshire Oaks; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: She has an attractive German pedigree and was bought for 550,000gns as a yearling; won at Newbury (1m, soft) last October on sole 2yo start and beaten about 3l by Amelia Earhart when third in the Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good) on last month's reappearance; she still looked a work in progress last time (slowly away and outpaced turning for home) and could have lots more to offer; slow ground might aid her cause; interesting.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Prominent runner winless since debut but classy form in Fillies' Mile, questionable soft ground record
runners_data.comment: Rallied for 3rd in 1,000 Guineas and it's possible this sizeable step up in trip will suit
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 since debut win on AW last June and unproven on slow ground; however, she was a fine second in a red-hot running of the Group 1 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket last October and reappeared with an excellent third in the 1,000 Guineas there (1m) last month; made the running on her last two starts; by Derby winner Masar and rallied in the closing stages last time, so it's possible that this sizeable step up in trip will suit; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Sugar Island
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with soft ground form but must prove she can sustain lead over this demanding track
runners_data.comment: Made all in 2yo Group 3 last October; work to do with two of these on Chester form
runners_data.spotlight: Third in Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last September and readily made all in Group 3 Staffordstown Stud Stakes at the Curragh (1m, heavy) in October; she could improve for last month's comeback run in the Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good) but has work to do with stablemate Amelia Earhart and A La Prochaine on that form; others preferred.

runners_data.name: K Sarra
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from strong Beckett team, stamina-bred but the 7f drop last time suggests pace concerns
runners_data.comment: Stayed on for third in the Musidora and could be a serious force over this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to connections' 10.2f/1m4f Group 2 winner Pride Of Arras; comfortable win at Southwell (1m, AW) last November on sole 2yo start and the drop to 7f was against her in the Fred Darling at Newbury (good) on her return; left that run well behind when staying on for third in the Group 3 Musidora at York (10.2f, good) last month, beaten just over 2l by Legacy Link; looks set to relish this step up in trip and she could be a serious force.

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with soft ground experience but inconsistent form pattern raises reliability questions
runners_data.comment: Won the Listed Cheshire Oaks by 2l and is following same route as 2025 winner Minnie Hauk
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon previous promise (including on soft ground) when easily winning a maiden at Leopardstown (1m, yielding) last October on her fifth start, and reappeared with 2l win in Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good) where she wore a hood and blinkers for the first time (retained today); she's followed the same route on her last two races as Minnie Hauk, who won this for Ballydoyle 12 months ago, and Ryan Moore rides; major player.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up significantly in class after Lingfield Listed win, stable in excellent form
runners_data.comment: Impressive in Lingfield trial; has a chance even though Ryan Moore rides Amelia Earhart
runners_data.spotlight: 7f maiden winner (soft to heavy) who took a big step forward with a convincing win in the Listed Oaks Trial at Lingfield (11.6f, good to firm) last month on her sixth start, which was her first run beyond 1m; Ryan Moore was on board last time and rides stablemate Amelia Earhart this afternoon, but she was certainly impressive at Lingfield and is unexposed at the trip; chance.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with recent course win but limited soft ground exposure and shortest price suggests overrated
runners_data.comment: Strong finish for Listed third over 1m2f at Goodwood; might not be a forlorn hope each-way
runners_data.spotlight: Won Wolverhampton novice (7f, AW) last October on third start and followed up on handicap/seasonal debut here (8.5f, good) in April; kept on strongly for 1l third in Listed Height Of Fashion Stakes at Goodwood (1m2f, good) 13 days ago; she has plenty to find on form but the step up in trip could prompt further improvement and she might not be a forlorn hope each-way.

races.paceDynamic: Sugar Island will dictate from the front with no genuine pace pressure, setting a measured gallop that should see her still travelling well turning for home. Four horses (Thundering On, Venetian Lace, Amelia Earhart, Cameo) all want prominent positions creating inevitable traffic problems 2-3 furlongs out as they fan wide or get squeezed for room. The hold-up quartet (Legacy Link, A La Prochaine, K Sarra, On Message) will have plenty of horse to aim at but face the challenge of making up significant ground on Epsom's unique contours. This pace setup strongly favours front-runners and those able to get first run from prominent positions, while making life difficult for horses relying on late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sugar Island Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sugar Island maintains her lead turning into the straight without serious challenge
scenarios.body: She can use Epsom's downhill run to stretch the field before the climb, with any prominently-placed horse getting first run having the edge over hold-up horses. The sustainable pace she sets makes it hard for closers to peg back those who travel smoothly into contention.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners clash for position approaching Tattenham Corner
scenarios.body: The pace quickens as they jostle, setting up the race for a closer with Sugar Island potentially weakening after battling. Hold-up horses with clear runs can capitalize on the earlier pace battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Sugar Island goes too slowly and gets swamped by the prominent group before halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint from 3f out with those getting clearest runs prevailing over those caught in traffic. Superior class tells in a rough finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Perfect Hold-Up Trip
scenarios.trigger: If Sugar Island sets genuine pace under pressure from prominent runners throughout
scenarios.body: The early pace battle sets up a perfect scenario for the hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders. Class and stamina become decisive factors.

watchPoints.text: Sugar Island could get loose on the lead if no prominent runner applies early pressure, making her very hard to catch
Venetian Lace and Thundering On may clash for the same prominent position, compromising both chances
Legacy Link needs the pace to be strong enough to set up her finishing kick on ground she's never encountered
Cameo represents the in-form O'Brien team but faces a significant class rise from Listed to Group 1 level
The three Beckett runners (A La Prochaine, K Sarra, On Message) could provide tactical complications if bunched together

races.name: HKJC World Pool Handicap

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won this race last year but faces stronger opposition and carries 6lb more weight
runners_data.comment: Won this last year off 6lb lower; won penultimate start and excuse latest; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who was 6lb lower when landing this race (good to soft) last season; this year's running is more competitive but his success in the Thirsk Hunt Cup (1m, good to firm) last month was close to a career best and he had a possible excuse when failing to back that up at York; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Popmaster
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with good soft ground record but needs luck from unfavorable draw in large field
runners_data.comment: Last effort, from poor draw, was better than it looks
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins include three on good to soft/soft; also won on AW at Kempton (1m) in February but only midfield in valuable events at Newcastle (AW) and Ascot (good) on his last two starts; however, latter effort was better than it looks having been poorly drawn.

runners_data.name: Thunder Roar
runners_data.note: Soft ground specialist holding-up but hasn't fired this season and needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Soft-ground specialist; down the weights & Colin Keane booking interesting; watch market
runners_data.spotlight: Soft-ground specialist who landed a fifth success when scoring at Ayr (1m) in September; yet to get going in three starts this year but he's edging down the weights and the booking of Colin Keane catches the eye; requires monitoring in the market with every drop of rain in his favour.

runners_data.name: Man Of La Mancha
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping in class after disappointing efforts, could benefit from easier company
runners_data.comment: Hampered latest; tactically versatile sort who is well drawn to sit handy; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded before winning at Windsor (good to firm) last May and finished that season with further wins at Sandown (also 1m, soft) and Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm); on the premises when he suffered chance-ending interference at Newbury last time and this tactically versatile sort is well drawn to sit handy; interesting.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Ex-French hold-up type making British debut for in-form Ian Williams, unknown quantity but interesting
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; 80-1 when down the field (1m, good) on his British debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French gelding who won four times there, the last two coming over 8.5f (AW) and 1m1f (good) at Chantilly last spring; changed hands for 75,000euros in November; 80-1 when 19th of 24 at Newbury (1m, good) in April on his British debut and he's probably one for further down the line.

runners_data.name: Bragbor
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who made late debut but has shown promise on artificial surfaces, turf step-up needed
runners_data.comment: Useful on AW but only seventh on turf debut last time; plenty of guesswork involved
runners_data.spotlight: He made his debut only as a 4yo but it was a winning one at Newcastle (1m); subsequently useful form on AW included another narrow win at that venue (1m2f) in August for George Scott and he went mighty close over latter C&D on stable debut in November; niggled along at various stages when seventh on his turf debut (10.5f) last month and some guesswork is involved as to whether this test will bring out the best in him.

runners_data.name: Nizam
runners_data.note: Another ex-French hold-up horse from Williams stable, flopped on British debut and others preferred
runners_data.comment: Similar profile to stablemate Ozat; others look more likely
runners_data.spotlight: He has a similar profile to stablemate Ozat, boasting good form in France but 80-1 when down the field in that same Newbury race on his British debut; others look more likely.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form with recent course win, Ryan Moore booking catches eye
runners_data.comment: Won 12th race when scoring last time; has never won off a mark this high, though
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile regarding ground and he was winning his 12th race when beating Jimmy Speaking and Final Night at Newmarket (1m, good) three weeks ago; that was a comfortable win and he has the assistance of Ryan Moore but this demands more from him (has never won off a mark this high).

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in career-best form who was only beaten by Sterling Knight last time out
runners_data.comment: Better than ever this season but he'll need more from this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on soft ground; better than ever this season, winning at Doncaster (good to soft) and following up at Southwell (again 7f, AW); solid second to Sterling Knight (1m, good) last time but he'll need more from the same mark.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who has never raced on soft ground, tactical advantage but ground query
runners_data.comment: Made all on return; not so good latest; unraced on softer than good but Murphy keeps faith
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on ground softer than good; Chester maiden (7.5f) winner who made all on Newmarket's July course last August; had been gelded when successfully repeating those tactics on his comeback at Newmarket (also 1m) in April but below that form back there at the Guineas meeting the following month; not dismissed, with Oisin Murphy sticking with him.

runners_data.name: Celeborn
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 343-day break but showed promise when winning on reappearance last year
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; fair return and drops back in trip in cheekpieces; unexposed; he's a player
runners_data.spotlight: Won on good to soft as a juvenile and reappeared with good-ground C&D success at last year's Spring meeting; that was his only start in 2025 and he made a respectable comeback despite hanging when fifth of 11 at Newbury (1m2f) three weeks ago; drops back down in trip with cheekpieces added and his best days are almost certainly ahead of him; player.

runners_data.name: Principality
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has won on heavy ground and dropping to favorable racing weight
runners_data.comment: Heavy-ground winner who won last time; 2lb nudge shouldn't stop him being competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Heavy-ground winner of a Glorious Goodwood handicap (1m) last July and he had dipped below that winning mark when scoring at Nottingham (8.5f, good) last time; 2lb nudge shouldn't stop him being competitive.

runners_data.name: Stem
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been campaigned over longer trips, return to mile could suit perfectly
runners_data.comment: Good second (1m, good to soft) on final start at three; respectable return; unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Wide-margin win (7f, heavy) on his sole start at two promised plenty and, after being campaigned over 1m2f and 1m4f, he recorded a clear career best when second of 15 over 1m at Newbury (good to soft) on his final start at three; subsequently gelded and his reappearance when beaten less than 4l at Newbury in April was perfectly respectable; unexposed and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer from same stable as Mirsky, has soft ground form and dropping in grade
runners_data.comment: It was this mark he raced from when well held at York three weeks ago; career best needed
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner who landed a third success at Pontefract (1m, good) on his penultimate start, having attracted support; also effective on a softer surface than that but it was this mark he raced from when well held at York three weeks ago and this demands a career best.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who made all when winning last time, consistent performer seeking back-to-back wins
runners_data.comment: Can go forward; has to put poor return behind him but that's not impossible
runners_data.spotlight: Proved progressive last year having joined this yard, winning three times (good to firm/AW) including when making all at Wolverhampton (8.5f) in July; also ran really well when second of 17 at Ascot (1m, soft; off current mark) in September but he was beaten a long way on his final start of that term and again at Lingfield on his reappearance four weeks ago; needs to put those efforts behind him but that's not out of the question.

runners_data.name: Hot Cash
runners_data.note: Prominent type with soft ground experience, light weight and David Probert 7lb claim helps chances
runners_data.comment: Course winner who was back near his best when second last time; far from dismissed
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on soft going; picked up a maiden here (7f, good) in July 2024 on his debut; fair run of form last year came to a crashing halt when virtually tailed off over C&D (good to soft) in September; subsequently gelded and he was back to near his best when second of 13 at Thirsk (1m, good) last time; far from dismissed.

runners_data.name: Asmen Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing blinkers for first time, consistent placer seeking breakthrough win
runners_data.comment: Soft conditions would ask a question but otherwise could go well in new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Salisbury maiden (1m2f, good to firm) last June when sporting first-time cheekpieces for previous yard; yet to score for current stable but he's been placed on six of those seven starts and it was a narrow defeat when second of ten at Windsor (1m, good to firm; visored) under Silvestre De Sousa latest; soft going would ask a question but he's well drawn to go forward and newly fitted blinkers might eke out more.

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better on artificial surfaces but showed improved form when third last time
runners_data.comment: Good efforts on turf last two starts; career-high mark to overcome though
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time AW winner who is 0-6 on turf but his 40-1 second of 13 at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) was a good effort in May and he backed it up when third to Sterling Knight over that C&D (good) a fortnight later; sole start on good to soft (1m2f) last year was inconclusive but he'll do well to defy this career-high mark.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Winston is the only confirmed front-runner, giving him a tactical advantage as he can dictate terms without early pressure from fellow leaders. Jimmy Speaking, Stem, Hot Cash, Mr Swivell and Asmen Warrior will sit prominent, but none are natural pace-forcers, meaning Winston can control the tempo. The large field of 18 runners features predominantly hold-up horses including Popmaster, Thunder Roar, Man Of La Mancha, Ozat, Bragbor, Nizam, Sterling Knight, Celeborn, Principality, Walsingham and Final Night, creating traffic problems in the back half. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and the lone leader, as they avoid the inevitable congestion behind and can utilize the controlled gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Winston gets an uncontested lead and dictates a steady pace
scenarios.body: Winston can save energy early then quicken when it matters, while the prominent runners like Jimmy Speaking and Stem get first run on the packed field behind. The large group of hold-up horses will struggle for racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Jimmy Speaking or Stem press Winston early, creating a stronger gallop
scenarios.body: The increased pace will set up the hold-up horses perfectly, particularly those with proven stamina like Sterling Knight and Man Of La Mancha who can finish strongly. The early leaders will weaken in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches up approaching the turn with multiple hold-up horses trapped
scenarios.body: Those positioned prominently like Hot Cash and Asmen Warrior will benefit from clear runs while proven operators like Celeborn and Walsingham get hampered. The race becomes about luck and positioning rather than pure ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Surge Special
scenarios.trigger: If Thunder Roar or Ozat produce exceptional late runs despite traffic
scenarios.body: The soft ground specialist Thunder Roar could weave through or the classy ex-French Ozat might have the gears to overcome positioning. This requires everything falling perfectly for a back-marker.

watchPoints.text: Mister Winston has never raced on ground softer than good and soft conditions could blunt his natural speed advantage
Thunder Roar is a soft ground specialist but has failed to fire in three starts this year despite favorable conditions
Sterling Knight arrives in excellent form with Ryan Moore booked and recent course experience favoring his chances
Traffic problems are inevitable with 18 runners and 11 hold-up horses likely to get squeezed for room
Both Ian Williams runners Ozat and Nizam are making British debuts and represent unknown quantities despite French form

races.name: Cygames Surrey Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Greek Mythology
runners_data.note: Progressive front-runner with course form but faces stamina test against older, more experienced rivals in testing conditions
runners_data.comment: Thrice-raced Irish colt who has progressive 7f form; sire won on this card in 2019
runners_data.spotlight: Sire landed the Woodcote on this card in 2019 en route to even better things; this is a thrice-raced Irish colt who has progressive 7f form, most recently 1l third in Listed race at Naas (good); strong credentials.

runners_data.name: Ardisia
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer but may have reached his ceiling and needs to prove he retains last season's ability
runners_data.comment: Not totally solid on 2026 form and has probably already reached his ceiling anyway
runners_data.spotlight: Picked up a lot of prize-money during a busy 2yo season but isn't totally solid on 2026 efforts and has probably already reached his ceiling anyway; seems unlikely defy a 3lb penalty and top weight.

runners_data.name: Postmodern
runners_data.note: Strong early pace likely but 91 days off track and stepping up to 7f for first time creates stamina doubts
runners_data.comment: Has two useful pieces of 6f form; ready for a crack at 7f; hood is fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Has two useful pieces of 6f form, namely an emphatic domestic win on debut and rallying second in Meydan handicap last time; gelded since; ready for a crack at 7f; possibilities if taking well to first-time hood.

runners_data.name: Ten Carat Harry
runners_data.note: Proven finisher with excellent recent Newmarket win but Saffie Osborne's 5lb claim crucial in tight contest
runners_data.comment: Productive, mostly over 6f; has bits of 7f form, including at Listed level
runners_data.spotlight: Productive gelding, mostly over 6f and on AW; prevailed by a neck in Newmarket handicap (good to firm) back on turf last time, taking record to 7-12; has bits of 7f form, including at Listed level; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Stellar Sunrise
runners_data.note: Disappointed last time but has strong course record and prominent style suits likely strong pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Bit disappointing last time but otherwise a broadly progressive colt
runners_data.spotlight: Bit disappointing in similar event at Newmarket last time but otherwise a broadly progressive colt and can't be written off; ready winner of useful handicap at Newbury (7f, good) in his only other start this term.

runners_data.name: Ellusive Butterfly
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist improving with racing experience and 5lb weight allowance provides significant advantage
runners_data.comment: Has some encouraging turf form but this task demands a personal best
runners_data.spotlight: AW scorer; 0-5 on turf but ran well in this year's Fred Darling and looked better than the bare form (met traffic issues) in York handicap most recently; this task seems to demand a personal best, however.

runners_data.name: Awaken
runners_data.note: Talented but 51 days absence following poor seasonal return creates reliability concerns despite previous Group form
runners_data.comment: Possible danger on these terms, provided she takes well to first-time hood
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well in Group events at Royal Ascot (6f) and Newmarket last season; posted a duck egg in the Nell Gwyn in sole run this term but looks a possible danger on these terms, provided she takes well to first-time hood.

runners_data.name: Northern Champion
runners_data.note: Proven overseas but returning to domestic competition after 69-day break questions current form level
runners_data.comment: Came up short in Group 1 last time when bidding for Meydan hat-tirck
runners_data.spotlight: Record is 3-6, most of those starts in non-domestic races; came up short in Group 1 last time when bidding for Meydan hat-trick; bit to prove back on home soil but very hard to dismiss on ratings.

runners_data.name: Assaranca
runners_data.note: Likely to set strong pace but significant class drop from handicap company suggests she may struggle for stamina
runners_data.comment: Won well last time but has the worst chance at the weights back up in class
runners_data.spotlight: Won well at Lingfield (7f, good to firm) most recently but that was only a handicap off a mark of 70 and everything panned out perfectly for her; has the worst chance at the weights back up in class.

races.paceDynamic: Greek Mythology, Postmodern and Assaranca will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with all three confirmed front-runners unlikely to give each other an easy time in a small field. The pace will be testing throughout the 7f trip on soft ground, putting stamina at a premium and creating opportunities for closers to pick up the pieces. Epsom's unique downhill configuration into Tattenham Corner will amplify the pace pressure before the climb to the finish. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay the trip and finish powerfully, while early leaders face a stamina examination.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Greek Mythology, Postmodern and Assaranca engage in early pace warfare
scenarios.body: The soft ground and testing gallop will find out the leaders' stamina reserves, allowing patient hold-up horses to sweep past in the final furlong. Ten Carat Harry and Ardisia are perfectly positioned to capitalize on their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gets first run and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: Greek Mythology's progressive profile suggests he could dictate terms if allowed to lead unchallenged, with his recent third over course and distance proving his effectiveness here. The class drop from Group company to Listed level suits his development curve.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent racers time their moves perfectly approaching Tattenham Corner
scenarios.body: Stellar Sunrise and Northern Champion can track the early pace without getting involved in the speed battle, positioning them ideally for sustained challenges. Both have the class and tactical speed to bridge from mid-pack when the race develops.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even stronger than expected and finds out all the fancied runners
scenarios.body: Ellusive Butterfly's hold-up style and improving form could see her benefit from a truly-run race where stamina becomes the decisive factor. Her trainer Karl Burke's 14-day record provides additional confidence in her preparation.

watchPoints.text: If Greek Mythology breaks slowly or gets shuffled back early, his front-running tactics become compromised and chances diminish significantly
Watch for Postmodern's jumping from the gates after his long absence, as early positioning will be crucial for his pace-setting role
Stellar Sunrise's early position will indicate connections' confidence after his disappointing Newmarket effort last time out
Ten Carat Harry needs clear running room in the straight as Epsom's camber can cause traffic problems for hold-up horses
Monitor the pace through the first two furlongs as exceptionally fast early fractions will set up the perfect storm for closers

races.name: Debenhams Handicap

runners_data.name: The Angel King
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who thrives on soft ground with two French wins on heavy/very soft, 30 days since last run could be ideal
runners_data.comment: Step back in right direction when sixth at Chester; forecast slower ground could be a plus
runners_data.spotlight: Two-time French winner (7f, very soft/good to soft) who took a step back in the right direction with close sixth of 13 at Chester (7.5f, good) last month on his second stable start; the forecast slower ground could be a positive today and he's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won this very race in 2021 on good to soft, solid recent Thirsk form suggests he's ready
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2021 and 2024 and this week's rain has been in his favour; dangerous mark
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in the Thirsk Hunt Cup (1m, good to firm) last month but promising reappearance there (7f, good) previously; won this race in 2021 (good to soft) and 2024 (good to soft) and was third last year (good to soft); this week's rain has been in his favour and he's on a dangerous mark.

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suited by strong pace but tight Chester track may not have suited last time
runners_data.comment: Chester may not have suited last time; he's on a handy mark on last season's best form
runners_data.spotlight: Not at the top of his game on either run this year but well backed at Chester last time, when the tight track may not have been ideal; on a handy mark on last season's best form and and he's not discounted.

runners_data.name: Dance In The Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can be difficult to settle, Oisin Murphy booking significant with 30-day break
runners_data.comment: Won on reappearance at Chester despite wide draw; could still have more left in the tank
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who can be difficult to settle but ran well in some quality handicaps last summer (including on good to soft; unraced on softer) and reappeared with a win at Chester (7f, good) last month; prevailed despite a wide draw and she could still have more left in the tank.

runners_data.name: Colombier
runners_data.note: Prominent style with strong French soft ground record, heavy Ascot defeat may have needed that run
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard when well beaten on stable debut; interesting to see if his backers return
runners_data.spotlight: Won four times on slow ground in France (7f-1m2f); returned from long absence with heavy defeat on last month's stable debut at Ascot (1m, good to firm) where he pulled hard; that run may have got the freshness out of him and it will be interesting to see if he's again strong in the betting.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 234-day break, cheekpieces removed and gelded since disappointing last run
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo who twice ran really well over C&D last summer; could be involved
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing last October on final 3yo start but the cheekpieces adopted that day are dispensed with and he's been gelded since; won over C&D (good) last July before very good efforts in defeat at Goodwood (7f, good to soft) and over C&D (good); retains potential and could be involved.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Prominent style but winless in 17 starts since June 2023, recent Newmarket form below par
runners_data.comment: On a long losing run and below par last time, but made good start for new yard previously
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 since winning in June 2023 on his second start and he was below par at Newmarket (7f, good) three weeks ago; however, prior to that he was runner-up on his first two starts for this yard (7f, good) and has an each-way shout if he's back on song; has shown promise on good to soft ground.

runners_data.name: Monarch's Gold
runners_data.note: Prominent 3yo stepping up in trip for first time, unexposed beyond 6f with good Chester form
runners_data.comment: Went close over 7.5f at Chester last month on first run beyond 6f; could be involved
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 3yo who went beyond 6f for the first time when going close at Chester (7.5f, good) last month; has also shown promise on good to soft ground; unexposed at this sort of trip and could be involved.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who impressed on stable debut at Pontefract, 37 days freshness ideal
runners_data.comment: Got up close home over 6f on stable debut and could have more to offer; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Considerable promise during light career for Karl Burke and better than ever when getting up close home in small field on his stable/seasonal debut at Pontefract (6f, good); there can be optimism that he will be fine back up to 7f and on slower ground, and he could have more to offer; contender.

runners_data.name: Crimson Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two course and distance wins, recent Goodwood victory suggests he handles current form
runners_data.comment: Two C&D wins and on the scoresheet at Goodwood a fortnight ago; could be bang there
runners_data.spotlight: Two C&D wins, the latest when completing a hat-trick last July (good to firm), and he won at Goodwood (7f, good) a fortnight ago; could be bang there if handling the forecast slow ground (mixed messages in his form).

runners_data.name: Pietro
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with progressive profile, March AW win shows he's maintained form through winter break
runners_data.comment: 4yo who has continued the good work this season and might not be far away
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive during last season's 3yo campaign and continued the good work when winning at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in March on his reappearance; another good run when third to Dance In The Storm at Chester (7f, good) last month; versatile ground-wise and might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Sunny Smile
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 275-day absence, last seen as 2yo but showed decent form
runners_data.comment: Promising 2yo last year but this is a tough starting point to his 3yo year
runners_data.spotlight: Won 2yo maiden at Hamilton (6f, good) last July on third outing and runner-up there (6f, good to soft) in September on second nursery start; that latest form was franked by the winner and every chance he'll continue to improve, but this is a tough starting point to his 3yo year; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Mister Bluebird
runners_data.note: Front-running 8yo in excellent spring form, short-headed at Musselburgh then second to Crimson Spirit
runners_data.comment: 8yo who has been as good as ever this spring, runner-up on last two starts; respected
runners_data.spotlight: 8yo who has been as good as ever this spring, short-headed at Musselburgh (7f, good) then second of 14 to Crimson Spirit at Goodwood (7f, good); last season's two wins came on soft ground; effective here; respected.

runners_data.name: A War Eagle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who made all at Beverley, needs to find extra improvement off recent form
runners_data.comment: Made all at Beverley on second stable start; fifth on next two outings but needs extra
runners_data.spotlight: Made all at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) in April on second stable start; respectable efforts when fifth on his next two outings but he needs something extra today and is unproven on slow ground.

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: Front-runner who made all to win course and distance on good to soft, 60-day break since seasonal return
runners_data.comment: This is more competitive than she's used to but this C&D winner is not ruled out each-way
runners_data.spotlight: Beat her five rivals to make all over C&D (good to soft) last September on final run for Andrew Balding; didn't run badly on stable/seasonal debut at Kempton (6f, AW) in April and could improve for that run; this race is more competitive than she's used to but she's not ruled out each-way.

runners_data.name: Zarathos
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with back-to-back wins at Windsor and York, 7lb rise may halt momentum
runners_data.comment: Took a long time to get off the mark but has won his last two and is clearly thriving
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the 18th attempt at Windsor (1m, good to firm) last month and followed up in big field at York (7f, good) eight days later; latest 7lb rise may not stop this thriving 4yo if he handles the softer ground here.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Bluebird and Musical Angel are the confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace, with Musical Angel having made all when winning over course and distance last September. Dance In The Storm can be difficult to settle and may also press forward from his prominent style, creating an honest gallop throughout. The decent early pace should set up the race for hold-up horses like The Angel King, Arctic Thunder, and Crimson Spirit who can use their finishing kicks. This pace dynamic clearly favours the hold-up merchants who can sit behind the genuine pace and deliver late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest between the front-runners
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will stretch the field and exhaust the prominent racers, allowing the patient hold-up horses to pick off tired leaders in the final furlong. The Angel King, Arctic Thunder, and Crimson Spirit all possess the tactical speed to capitalize when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent horse can secure the perfect position behind the leaders
scenarios.body: A horse like Dance In The Storm or Monarch's Gold can track the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle, then strike when the front-runners weaken. Their prominent style allows them to be close enough to capitalize without doing too much early work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too fierce between Mister Bluebird and Musical Angel
scenarios.body: One of them may get a soft lead as the other fades early, allowing the survivor to dictate terms and hold on. Musical Angel's course and distance win suggests she knows how to handle this track when getting her own way.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners go off too fast and fade before halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical with no clear pace-setter, favoring horses that can quicken from any position. This would suit versatile types who don't depend on a strong pace to be effective.

watchPoints.text: Musical Angel and Mister Bluebird must be monitored for how fierce their early battle becomes as it will determine the entire race shape
Dance In The Storm's settling behavior early on as Oisin Murphy may struggle to get him to relax behind the pace
The Angel King's position turning for home as he needs to be within striking distance to use his proven soft ground finishing kick
Monarch's Gold stepping up in trip for the first time as the extra furlong is unknown territory for this lightly raced 3yo
Arctic Thunder's position choice early as the hold-up horse needs to avoid getting trapped behind a wall of horses on the turn
